findings.what: The S0 choice for the running-champion UP test (02:02Z (2)) can hide a real UP. R34-A1 says that for exp89p 'S0 = any snapshot with count 53 and display 0.959 (e.g. 20260929T0513Z)'. tools/uptest.py compare counts only the teams that were above us IN S0 and are below us in S1, and public bests never fall. A newer S0 therefore holds a superset of the teams above us and is strictly more sensitive. Between 05:13Z and 07:13Z our rank went from 133 to 136, so 3 teams entered the 0.959 block above us. These are exactly the teams a marginally higher exp89p would pass, and an S0 of 0513Z cannot see them, so k is biased toward 0 and the champion exp87a stays by default. A second gap: the save jobs run at the first COMPLETE header, and nothing handles a leaderboard that lags the submissions API. If post_exp89p still shows count 53, compare prints 'no UP'. Under the '+1 exactly' rule that reads as MASKED, and the champion stays. The lag has not happened so far: at 21:42Z and 12:14Z the LB count was already up at the header. Neither save() nor compare() checks the counts.

Run 'timeout 180 python tools/uptest.py save post_<token>_b' once, 5 min later, and use that as S1. Code MASKED only on a count move of 2 or more with equal displays (logged +2 rule), never on +0. Log the S0/S1 tags, both counts and k in the read line.
